answer: An agent harbor can require every registered public key to burn 10 onyx tokens before opening a job thread. A smart contract verifies the irreversible burn and binds its receipt to one key, preventing receipt reuse. Creating 1,000 identities destroys 10,000 tokens, imposing a verifiable cost per identity. This deters cheap flooding, but wealthy attackers can still buy identities, and token price drops weaken the barrier.
